ExifTool.coverage: All recognized tags, duplicate tags, unknown tags and unknown binary tags; complete group families 0–6; embedded document extraction through level 3; structured values. Embedded fields from EXIF, XMP, IPTC, GPS, JFIF, ICC, Photoshop, PNG, GIF and QuickTime groups were included where present.

metadata_scope_and_limits: ExifTool 13.60 was fetched from the official source repository at the pinned commit recorded above. All recognized tags, unknown text tags and unknown binary tags were requested across group families 0–6, with duplicate and embedded-tag extraction enabled.
The two Photoshop APP13 blocks contain a zero-byte IPTC dataset and an IPTCDigest equal to the MD5 of empty data; ExifTool also decodes this. There is no opaque Photoshop path-info resource.

ExifTool reports one 28-byte QuickTime Unknown_edts field. Verbose output shows a standard edts/elst box with one timing entry (51.6 seconds, media time 1024, rate 1.0); this is structural timeline data, not free-form user metadata.

The MP4 encoded MediaData and codec/sample tables are video payload and structural timing data, not user-authored metadata. ffprobe and ExifTool found one video stream, no audio/attachment stream and no chapters.

File, Composite and ExifTool-generated groups are excluded from embedded-file findings. An all-tags RequestAll=3 pass attempted macOS Spotlight extraction and logged an mdls warning; the embedded group/field results exactly match the clean pass with MDItemTags disabled.

This remains a bounded file-metadata audit, not a review of visible screenshot contents, every pixel/frame, arbitrary steganography or metadata outside the recognized/unknown binary sections exposed by the tools.
metadata_result: ExifTool 13.60 and the independent parsers found no author/contact/GPS/location/device-serial/credential/bearer metadata values in the supported embedded fields. Standard color-profile copyright is Google Inc. 2016; media tags are standard container/encoder identifiers. The one automated location-keyword flag is only the technical MP4 chroma_location field. This is bounded metadata evidence, not unconditional privacy certification.
